title: Data Visualisation
description: Choose the right chart for a specific audience and cadence, and defend the choice. Tests metric selection, visual design, and executive communication.

seo.overviewBody: Data visualization transforms numbers into visual insights. Employers seek analysts who understand visualization principles: choosing appropriate chart types (line, bar, scatter, heatmap), configuring accessible color palettes, and avoiding misleading axes.

deliverables.title: 1. Exploratory Data Visualization Deck
deliverables.desc: Portfolio presentation showcasing chart visualisations paired with analytical commentary.

deliverables.title: 2. Custom Chart Code / BI Dashboard
deliverables.desc: Clean Matplotlib/Seaborn/Plotly Python scripts or interactive BI visual charts.

deliverables.title: 3. Visualization Principles Audit
deliverables.desc: Self-audit evaluating chart contrast ratios, axis scale integrity, and visual legibility.

faqs.question: When should you use a line chart versus a bar chart?
faqs.answer: Line charts are designed for continuous time-series trends over time, whereas bar charts are optimal for comparing discrete categorical groups.

faqs.question: Why should bar chart Y-axes always start at zero?
faqs.answer: Truncating the Y-axis on bar charts exaggerates relative size differences between categories, misleading stakeholders about true proportions.

faqs.question: How do you ensure data visualisations are colorblind accessible?
faqs.answer: Use colorblind-safe palettes (like Viridis or Okabe-Ito) and avoid relying solely on red/green contrast to convey status.
